To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified ZNRF3 as a gene that influences cell survival in the context of antitubulin therapy.

the antitumoral drugs paclitaxil and colchicin inhibit cell growth and that the drug concentrations that affect tubulin polymerization in cells are hundreds of times larger than the clinically useful levels.
genetic screening of the human genome identified ZNRF3 as the dominant genetic locus affecting the response of cells to the antitubulins paclitaxol and colchicine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a genetic screen to identify genes involved in the action of antitubulin agents and the subsequent validation of one of the hits.
the identification of genes and proteins that mediate drug action.
the genetic and biochemical mechanisms of action of antitubulin agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ZNRF3 is a genetic target for antitubulin action, but the mechanism of drug action is not through the Wnt pathway.
ZNRF3 is a key regulator of Wnt signaling and that it is also a genetic determinant of the cellular responses to antitubulin compounds.
ZNRF3 is a genetic target that mediates drug action at therapeutic concentrations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antitumor drug, paclitaxed, and the antitumor agent, colchicine, both affect Wnt signaling, which is important for cell survival.
ZNRF3, a Wnt signaling inhibitor, is a key genetic target for the antitubulins.
ZNRF3 is a novel genetic target for antitubulin therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genetic mapping of drug targets is a viable method to discover new mechanisms of action for drugs that have been in use for decades.
the genetic screen identified a novel mechanism of action for antitubulin compounds and a potential therapeutic application for Wnt-C59 in cancer treatment.
genetic screening can identify drug targets that are relevant for drug action at clinically relevant concentrations.
